content:
In FLT we made use of semialgebra maps, the algebra analogue of semilinear maps, which are maps f : A →+* B between an R-algebra A and an S-algebra B such that, for some φ : R →+* S, the following diagram commutes:

f : A --------→ B
    ↑           ↑
    |           |
φ : R --------→ S

i.e., f (algebraMap R A r) = algebraMap S B (φ r). I have tried upstreaming this using two different approaches.

  1. Make AlgHom a special case (#38376). This approach mirrors the semilinear map case and refactors AlgHom in a mathlib PR so that it is defined as a semialgebra map. One recovers the original AlgHom using RingHom.id R for φ. However, this led to non-trivial technical debt, which can be found in the radar results of #38376. While I was able to improve some of this, it remains unclear to me whether the rest of this debt is an unavoidable consequence of the increased number of instance hypotheses in the refactor (for example AlgHom.comp now has four base rings + instances).

  2. Define SemialgHom as a separate type (#43351). As it appears in FLT, this PR keeps SemialgHom as a separate type and defines transfers to AlgHom in the RingHom.id R case. This led to essentially no technical debt, although it means more API and diverges from the semilinear map case.

Are there opinions on which approach is preferred? The second seems preferable to me based on performance, but perhaps there are ways to improve the technical debt of approach 1 further which would avoid the duplication of approach 2.
